namespace Erdos582

/--
A graph `G` is *edge-Ramsey for triangles* (in arrow notation, $G \to (K_3, K_3)^e$) if any
$2$-colouring of the edges of `G` produces a monochromatic $K_3$: three pairwise adjacent
vertices whose three connecting edges all receive the same colour.
-/
def EdgeRamseyTriangle {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : G.edgeSet → Fin 2,
    ∃ (u v w : V) (huv : G.Adj u v) (hvw : G.Adj v w) (huw : G.Adj u w),
      c ⟨s(u, v), huv⟩ = c ⟨s(v, w), hvw⟩ ∧ c ⟨s(v, w), hvw⟩ = c ⟨s(u, w), huw⟩

/--
Does there exist a graph $G$ which contains no $K_4$, and yet any $2$-colouring of the edges
produces a monochromatic $K_3$?

Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa67] first asked for the existence of any such graph. Existence was proved
by Folkman [Fo70], but with very poor quantitative bounds. (As a result these quantities are
often called Folkman numbers.) The current best bounds on the minimal number of vertices $N$ of
such a graph are $21 \leq N \leq 786$, where the lower bound is due to Bikov and Nenov [BiNe20]
and the upper bound is due to Lange, Radziszowski, and Xu [LRX14].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos582.lean"]
theorem erdos_582 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (V : Type*) (_ : Fintype V) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.CliqueFree 4 ∧ EdgeRamseyTriangle G := by
  sorry

end Erdos582

reformulations.difference: The original Erdős–Hajnal question, quoted in Lange–Radziszowski–Xu §1, asks for a K₄-free graph that is not the union of two triangle-free graphs. Lean instead requires every two-colouring of its edges to contain a monochromatic triangle, as does erdosproblems.com.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A colouring without monochromatic triangles partitions the edges into two triangle-free spanning graphs whose union is G. Conversely, if G is a union of two triangle-free graphs, assign each edge to one graph containing it; overlapping edges can be assigned arbitrarily. Both colour classes remain triangle-free. Negating these equivalent existence statements gives the Ramsey predicate. The predicate equivalence and the finite-graph existential equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms.

review.notes:
Both declarations are faithful. EdgeRamseyTriangle colours actual unordered edges; its adjacency witnesses force three distinct vertices. I proved its equivalence to a genuine 3-clique in a colour-class graph, excluded edgeless witnesses, and evaluated complete graphs of orders 0–6: the predicate is false through order 5 and true at order 6. Fintype enforces finiteness, and an additional Lean equivalence verifies that the universe-polymorphic existential is equivalent to using graphs on Fin n. answer(True) and research solved correctly record Folkman’s affirmative solution. The numerical challenges in the sources are separate from the qualitative existence question stated here.

The live erdosproblems.com page was blocked, so I used its archived statement and independent primary literature. The May 2026 paper confirms the docstring’s bounds. For the linked proof, I proved equivalence of its Bool-colouring/cliqueNum = 3 condition with the file’s condition. Its source contains no sorry or custom axioms. Independent kernel certification under its pinned Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 environment was not completed: replay against the available 4.33.1 environment encounters compatibility errors, which are not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
